questions.subject: bio
questions.q: Which of the following is the largest current cause of biodiversity loss on land?
questions.hint: Think about land-use change for agriculture.

questions.subject: bio
questions.q: What term means conservation of a species in its natural habitat? (two words)
questions.hint: It is Latin for 'in place'.

questions.subject: bio
questions.q: What term means conservation of a species outside its natural habitat, for example in a zoo or seed bank? (two words)
questions.hint: It is Latin for 'out of place'.

questions.subject: bio
questions.q: Which is an example of ex situ conservation?
options: A seed bank storing frozen seeds
questions.answer: A seed bank storing frozen seeds
questions.hint: Which option keeps material away from the wild habitat?

questions.subject: bio
questions.q: What is the main purpose of a wildlife corridor?
options: To connect fragmented habitats so populations can move and interbreed
questions.answer: To connect fragmented habitats so populations can move and interbreed
questions.hint: Think about isolated populations.

questions.subject: bio
questions.q: Which term describes a species introduced to an area where it spreads and harms native species?
questions.hint: It is not native and causes damage.

questions.subject: bio
questions.q: Why is overexploitation a threat to biodiversity?
options: Organisms are harvested faster than populations can recover
questions.answer: Organisms are harvested faster than populations can recover
questions.hint: Think of overfishing.

questions.subject: bio
questions.q: Why are small captive populations at risk even in zoos?
questions.hint: Think about the gene pool.

questions.subject: bio
questions.q: Which is an advantage of in situ conservation?
options: Species keep interacting with their ecosystem and evolving naturally
It protects species from all threats
It is always cheaper than any other method
questions.answer: Species keep interacting with their ecosystem and evolving naturally
questions.hint: Think about the whole ecosystem.

questions.subject: bio
questions.q: What is a 'biodiversity hotspot'?
options: A region with high endemism that is under significant threat
questions.answer: A region with high endemism that is under significant threat
questions.hint: Two conditions define it.

questions.subject: bio
questions.q: Which practice can help reintroduce a captive-bred species successfully?
options: Restoring the habitat and removing the original threat first
questions.answer: Restoring the habitat and removing the original threat first
questions.hint: Why did the species decline in the first place?

questions.subject: bio
questions.q: What is an 'edge effect' in a fragmented habitat?
options: Changed conditions at the boundary that affect species living there
A rise in biodiversity in the core
The total area of the forest
questions.answer: Changed conditions at the boundary that affect species living there
questions.hint: Small fragments have more boundary relative to their area.

questions.subject: bio
questions.q: A rainforest reserve originally covering 1200 km² has lost 18% of its area. What area, in km², remains?
questions.hint: Find 18% and subtract it.

questions.subject: bio
questions.q: Why is the EDGE of Existence approach used to prioritise species?
options: It combines evolutionary distinctiveness with how endangered a species is
questions.answer: It combines evolutionary distinctiveness with how endangered a species is
questions.hint: EDGE is an acronym of two ideas.

questions.subject: bio
questions.q: Evaluate, in 3–5 sentences, the use of ex situ conservation compared with in situ conservation for an endangered species.
questions.hint: Consider genetic diversity, cost, habitat and the chance of reintroduction.

questions.subject: bio
questions.q: Explain, in 3–5 sentences, how human activities have contributed to the current biodiversity crisis, sometimes called a sixth mass extinction.
questions.hint: Mention at least three different causes.

questions.subject: bio
questions.q: Which gas makes the largest contribution to the enhanced greenhouse effect caused by humans?
questions.hint: It is released by burning fossil fuels.

questions.subject: bio
questions.q: What does the enhanced greenhouse effect mean?
options: Extra greenhouse gases from human activity trap more heat, raising global temperatures
The natural warming without which Earth would be frozen
questions.answer: Extra greenhouse gases from human activity trap more heat, raising global temperatures
questions.hint: 'Enhanced' means added to the natural effect.

questions.subject: bio
questions.q: Greenhouse gases absorb mainly which type of radiation emitted by the Earth's surface?
questions.hint: The surface re-emits energy at longer wavelengths.

questions.subject: bio
questions.q: Besides carbon dioxide, name another greenhouse gas released by cattle and rice paddies.
questions.hint: Its formula has one carbon and four hydrogens.

questions.subject: bio
questions.q: What is a 'range shift'?
options: A change in the geographical area where a species lives
A change in a species' diet only
A change in the length of a day
questions.answer: A change in the geographical area where a species lives
questions.hint: Species may move towards the poles or uphill.

questions.subject: bio
questions.q: As temperatures rise, many species are observed moving…
options: towards the poles and to higher altitudes
towards the equator and lower altitudes
questions.answer: towards the poles and to higher altitudes
questions.hint: They follow cooler conditions.

questions.subject: bio
questions.q: Why does coral bleaching happen in warmer seas?
options: Corals expel their symbiotic algae under heat stress
questions.answer: Corals expel their symbiotic algae under heat stress
questions.hint: The algae give corals colour and food.

questions.subject: bio
questions.q: Melting Arctic sea ice is a threat to which animal that hunts from the ice?
questions.hint: It hunts seals from the ice.

questions.subject: bio
questions.q: What term means the long-term capture and storage of carbon, for example by forests or peat? (two words)
questions.hint: Plants do this through photosynthesis.

questions.subject: bio
questions.q: Which action increases carbon sequestration?
questions.hint: Which option adds growing plants?

questions.subject: bio
questions.q: Why does thawing permafrost create positive feedback on climate change?
options: It releases stored CO₂ and methane, causing more warming
questions.answer: It releases stored CO₂ and methane, causing more warming
questions.hint: Positive feedback amplifies the original change.

questions.subject: bio
questions.q: What evidence from ice cores is used to study past climate?
options: Trapped air bubbles show past CO₂ concentrations
Ice cores record wind speed directly
questions.answer: Trapped air bubbles show past CO₂ concentrations
questions.hint: Ancient air is preserved in the ice.

questions.subject: bio
questions.q: Atmospheric CO₂ rose from about 280 ppm before industrialisation to about 420 ppm today. What is the percentage increase? Give your answer to the nearest whole number.
questions.hint: Percentage increase = change ÷ original × 100.

questions.subject: bio
questions.q: A mismatch in timing between when caterpillars are most abundant and when birds hatch their chicks is an example of…
questions.hint: Phenology is about the timing of seasonal events.

questions.subject: bio
questions.q: Evaluate, in 3–5 sentences, the evidence that climate change is affecting ecosystems.
questions.hint: Use examples such as range shifts, coral bleaching and timing changes.

questions.subject: bio
questions.q: Discuss, in 3–5 sentences, the advantages and limitations of reforestation as a way to mitigate climate change.
questions.hint: Consider carbon storage, time, land use and permanence.

bus-hl.topic: IA: analysing the organization through the conceptual lens — HL: research and development

questions.subject: bus
questions.q: In the IB Business Management IA, what is the main difference between description and analysis?
options: Analysis explains causes, effects and significance using evidence
Analysis repeats facts from the documents
questions.answer: Analysis explains causes, effects and significance using evidence
questions.hint: Ask 'why' and 'so what?'.

questions.subject: bus
questions.q: How many key concepts can be chosen as the conceptual lens of the IA?
questions.hint: The IA focuses on a single lens.

questions.subject: bus
questions.q: Which business tool is most suitable for analysing internal strengths and weaknesses and external opportunities and threats?
questions.hint: Its name is an acronym of four words.

questions.subject: bus
questions.q: A student writes: 'The company's revenue was $2m in 2024.' What is missing to make this analysis?
options: An explanation of what the figure shows and why it matters for the research question
questions.answer: An explanation of what the figure shows and why it matters for the research question
questions.hint: Link evidence to the question.

questions.subject: bus
questions.q: What is the legal right that protects a new invention for a limited period, usually around 20 years?
questions.hint: It is registered with a government office.

questions.subject: bus
questions.q: Which form of intellectual property protects a brand name or logo?
questions.hint: Think of the ™ or ® symbol.

questions.subject: bus
questions.q: Which form of intellectual property protects original creative works such as books or software code?
questions.hint: Think of the © symbol.

questions.subject: bus
questions.q: Which is an example of 'process innovation'?
options: Introducing robots to speed up production
Launching a new flavour of drink
questions.answer: Introducing robots to speed up production
questions.hint: It changes how something is made.

questions.subject: bus
questions.q: Which is an example of 'product innovation'?
options: Launching a smartphone with a new foldable screen
questions.answer: Launching a smartphone with a new foldable screen
questions.hint: It changes what is sold.

questions.subject: bus
questions.q: What is 'incremental innovation'?
options: Small, gradual improvements to existing products or processes
questions.answer: Small, gradual improvements to existing products or processes
questions.hint: Think of version 2.0 of something.

questions.subject: bus
questions.q: Why might a firm spend heavily on research and development (R&D)?
options: To gain a competitive advantage through new or better products
To reduce all its costs immediately
Because it is required by every government
questions.answer: To gain a competitive advantage through new or better products
questions.hint: Think long-term.

questions.subject: bus
questions.q: Which is a disadvantage of high R&D spending?
options: High costs with no guarantee of success
questions.answer: High costs with no guarantee of success
questions.hint: Many projects fail.

questions.subject: bus
questions.q: In the IA, supporting documents should mainly be…
options: secondary sources relevant to the research question
questions.answer: secondary sources relevant to the research question
questions.hint: The IA is based on real organisational evidence.

questions.subject: bus
questions.q: Explain, in 3–5 sentences, how a student could use a SWOT analysis analytically, rather than descriptively, in the IA.
questions.hint: Link each point to evidence and to the research question; prioritise.

questions.subject: bus
questions.q: Discuss, in 3–5 sentences, whether patents encourage or limit innovation in an industry.
questions.hint: Consider incentives for inventors and barriers for competitors.

questions.subject: bus
questions.q: Which of these is one of the key concepts used as a conceptual lens in the IB Business IA?
questions.hint: There are four concepts; one of them is about long-term environmental and social impact.

bus-sl.topic: IA: analysing the organization through the conceptual lens

questions.subject: bus
questions.q: What is the role of the research question in the IB Business IA?
options: It focuses the analysis on a real issue facing the organisation
It must be about a fictional company
questions.answer: It focuses the analysis on a real issue facing the organisation
questions.hint: Every paragraph should connect back to it.

questions.subject: bus
questions.q: Which of these is NOT one of the IB Business key concepts?
questions.hint: The four are change, creativity, ethics and sustainability.

questions.subject: bus
questions.q: Which sentence is analysis rather than description?
options: Falling sales suggest that the new pricing strategy reduced demand among price-sensitive customers
The CEO's office is in the city centre
questions.answer: Falling sales suggest that the new pricing strategy reduced demand among price-sensitive customers
questions.hint: Look for cause and effect.

questions.subject: bus
questions.q: Which tool helps analyse the external environment using political, economic, social and technological factors?
questions.hint: It is an acronym of external factors.

questions.subject: bus
questions.q: Which tool helps a firm choose a growth strategy between market penetration, product development, market development and diversification?
questions.hint: It is a 2×2 matrix of products and markets.

questions.subject: bus
questions.q: Which tool weighs driving forces against restraining forces for a change?
questions.hint: Forces push for and against.

questions.subject: bus
questions.q: Why is it important to link evidence to the conceptual lens?
options: It shows how the concept helps explain the organisation's issue
It is only needed in the title
questions.answer: It shows how the concept helps explain the organisation's issue
questions.hint: The lens should shape the analysis.

questions.subject: bus
questions.q: A student only copies charts from supporting documents without commentary. What is the main weakness?
options: There is no interpretation of what the evidence means
questions.answer: There is no interpretation of what the evidence means
questions.hint: Data needs explanation.

questions.subject: bus
questions.q: Which is the best example of using 'change' as a conceptual lens?
options: Analysing how a café adapted its business model after customers moved to online ordering
questions.answer: Analysing how a café adapted its business model after customers moved to online ordering
questions.hint: Look for an organisation responding to something new.

questions.subject: bus
questions.q: What should a strong IA conclusion do?
options: Answer the research question based on the analysis
Repeat the introduction word for word
questions.answer: Answer the research question based on the analysis
questions.hint: It closes the argument.

questions.subject: bus
questions.q: Complete the analytical phrase often used to move from evidence to meaning: 'This suggests ______…' (one word that links to the implication)
questions.hint: It introduces a clause.

questions.subject: bus
questions.q: Which is a limitation of secondary supporting documents?
options: They may be biased or out of date
questions.answer: They may be biased or out of date
questions.hint: Consider who wrote them and when.

questions.subject: bus
questions.q: A firm's revenue grew from $400,000 to $460,000. What is the percentage growth?
questions.hint: Change ÷ original × 100.

questions.subject: bus
questions.q: Why is it useful to combine more than one business tool in the IA?
options: Different tools give complementary perspectives on the issue
questions.answer: Different tools give complementary perspectives on the issue
questions.hint: Triangulation strengthens conclusions.

questions.subject: bus
questions.q: Explain, in 3–5 sentences, how you would turn a descriptive sentence about a company's falling profits into analysis.
questions.hint: Add causes, consequences and a link to your research question.

questions.subject: bus
questions.q: Discuss, in 3–5 sentences, how choosing 'sustainability' as a conceptual lens could change the analysis of a fast-fashion retailer.
questions.hint: Think about environmental, social and economic impacts.

questions.subject: chem
questions.q: A compound shows a strong, broad IR absorption at 2500–3300 cm⁻¹ and a sharp one at about 1710 cm⁻¹. Which functional group is present?
questions.hint: The broad band is O–H; the sharp band is C=O.

questions.subject: chem
questions.q: In a mass spectrum, what does the molecular ion peak (M⁺) give?
options: The relative molecular mass of the compound
questions.answer: The relative molecular mass of the compound
questions.hint: It is the peak at the highest m/z for the intact molecule.

questions.subject: chem
questions.q: How many distinct hydrogen environments are there in ethanol, CH₃CH₂OH, in its ¹H NMR spectrum?
questions.hint: Count CH₃, CH₂ and OH.

questions.subject: chem
questions.q: In ¹H NMR, what does the integration (area under a peak) tell you?
options: The relative number of hydrogens in that environment
questions.answer: The relative number of hydrogens in that environment
questions.hint: It is a ratio.

questions.subject: chem
questions.q: Using the n+1 rule, a peak split into a quartet has how many hydrogens on adjacent carbon atoms?

questions.subject: chem
questions.q: Which reference standard is used to set 0 ppm in ¹H NMR?
questions.hint: It has 12 equivalent hydrogens and one signal.

questions.subject: chem
questions.q: A compound C₃H₆O shows a sharp IR band at 1715 cm⁻¹ and only ONE singlet in its ¹H NMR spectrum. Which is it?
questions.hint: Two identical CH₃ groups with no neighbouring H.

questions.subject: chem
questions.q: Propanal, CH₃CH₂CHO, has a ¹H NMR signal near 9–10 ppm. Which hydrogen causes it?
questions.hint: This environment is strongly deshielded.

questions.subject: chem
questions.q: A mass spectrum has M⁺ at m/z = 74. A fragment appears at m/z = 59. What mass, in mass units, has been lost?
questions.hint: Subtract the two values.

questions.subject: chem
questions.q: A fragment lost from a molecule with a mass of 15 most likely corresponds to which group? (give its formula)
questions.hint: It is the smallest alkyl group.

questions.subject: chem
questions.q: What information does the index of hydrogen deficiency (IHD) of a formula give?
options: The number of rings and/or π bonds
questions.answer: The number of rings and/or π bonds
questions.hint: It is also called degree of unsaturation.

questions.subject: chem
questions.q: Calculate the index of hydrogen deficiency (IHD) for C₄H₈O.
questions.hint: IHD = (2C + 2 − H)/2, ignoring O.

questions.subject: chem
questions.q: An unknown compound C₂H₄O₂ has a broad IR band at 2500–3300 cm⁻¹, a band at 1710 cm⁻¹ and two singlets in ¹H NMR with ratio 3:1. What is it?
questions.hint: Combine the O–H, C=O and the singlet data.

questions.subject: chem
questions.q: Why is it better to combine IR, MS and ¹H NMR rather than rely on one technique?
options: Each gives different, complementary information about the structure
One technique always gives wrong results
IR alone can always identify isomers
questions.answer: Each gives different, complementary information about the structure
questions.hint: IR: groups; MS: mass; NMR: hydrogen environments.

questions.subject: chem
questions.q: In ¹H NMR, an –OH proton in an alcohol often appears as which type of signal?
options: A singlet, because it rarely couples with neighbours
questions.answer: A singlet, because it rarely couples with neighbours
questions.hint: Exchange of the O–H proton removes splitting.

questions.subject: chem
questions.q: A compound C₃H₈O shows a broad IR band at 3200–3600 cm⁻¹ and three ¹H NMR signals with integration 6:1:1. Deduce its structure and justify it with the evidence (3–5 sentences).
questions.hint: Think about which isomer has two equivalent CH₃ groups.

questions.subject: chem
questions.q: Which region of an IR spectrum would show a C=O stretch?
questions.hint: Carbonyl bands are strong and sharp.

questions.subject: chem
questions.q: A broad IR absorption around 3200–3600 cm⁻¹ indicates which bond?
questions.hint: Hydrogen bonding makes it broad.

questions.subject: chem
questions.q: What does the 'fingerprint region' (below about 1500 cm⁻¹) help with?
options: Identifying a specific compound by comparison with known spectra
questions.answer: Identifying a specific compound by comparison with known spectra
questions.hint: Each molecule has a unique pattern there.

questions.subject: chem
questions.q: The molecular ion peak of a compound is at m/z = 46. What is its relative molecular mass?
questions.hint: The M⁺ peak corresponds to the whole molecule.

questions.subject: chem
questions.q: Which compound has a molecular ion at m/z = 58?

questions.subject: chem
questions.q: How many distinct hydrogen environments does propanone, CH₃COCH₃, have?
questions.hint: Are the two methyl groups equivalent?

questions.subject: chem
questions.q: How many ¹H NMR signals would you expect for methyl ethanoate, CH₃COOCH₃?
questions.hint: The two CH₃ groups are in different environments.

questions.subject: chem
questions.q: In ¹H NMR, the chemical shift (δ) depends mainly on…
options: the chemical environment of the hydrogen
the number of carbon atoms in the sample tube
questions.answer: the chemical environment of the hydrogen
questions.hint: Nearby electronegative atoms change it.

questions.subject: chem
questions.q: Ethanol shows ¹H NMR integration in the ratio…
questions.hint: Count hydrogens in CH₃, CH₂ and OH.

questions.subject: chem
questions.q: What is the name of the standard compound used as the 0 ppm reference in ¹H NMR? (abbreviation)
questions.hint: It is a silicon compound with four methyl groups.

questions.subject: chem
questions.q: A compound with formula C₂H₆O shows NO broad O–H band in IR and only one signal in ¹H NMR. What is it?
questions.hint: It is an ether isomer of ethanol.

questions.subject: chem
questions.q: Calculate the index of hydrogen deficiency (IHD) for C₂H₄.

questions.subject: chem
questions.q: An IHD of 4 for C₆H₆ suggests which structure?
options: A ring with three double bonds (benzene)
questions.answer: A ring with three double bonds (benzene)
questions.hint: Each ring or π bond counts as 1.

questions.subject: chem
questions.q: Which technique is best for identifying the functional groups present?
questions.hint: It detects bond vibrations.

questions.subject: chem
questions.q: Which piece of evidence best distinguishes propanal from propanone?
options: A ¹H NMR signal at about 9–10 ppm for the –CHO hydrogen
questions.answer: A ¹H NMR signal at about 9–10 ppm for the –CHO hydrogen
questions.hint: Both share the C=O and the same mass.

questions.subject: chem
questions.q: A compound has M⁺ at m/z = 60, a broad IR band at 2500–3300 cm⁻¹, a band at 1710 cm⁻¹ and two ¹H NMR singlets with ratio 3:1. Deduce the structure and justify it (3–5 sentences).
questions.hint: Use each technique in turn: mass, functional group, hydrogen environments.

comp-hl.topic: IA: final submission and academic integrity

questions.subject: comp
questions.q: A checklist before final submission should mainly confirm that:
options: all required components are present and consistent with each other
the program has as many lines as possible
questions.answer: all required components are present and consistent with each other
questions.hint: Documentation, product and video must tell the same story.

questions.subject: comp
questions.q: Which term names the IB principle of producing honest, properly acknowledged work? (two words)
questions.hint: There is an IB policy with this name.

questions.subject: comp
questions.q: You used an open-source library for encryption. Which acknowledgement is most complete?
options: Name the library, state its source and licence, and explain what it does in your solution
Only mention it if the moderator asks
List it in the file name
questions.answer: Name the library, state its source and licence, and explain what it does in your solution
questions.hint: A good citation lets a reader find and understand the source.

questions.subject: comp
questions.q: Why is it important to show clearly which parts of the code you wrote and which come from libraries?
options: Credit for complexity and ingenuity can only be given for your own work
It makes the program run faster
questions.answer: Credit for complexity and ingenuity can only be given for your own work
questions.hint: What exactly is being assessed?

questions.subject: comp
questions.q: What one-word term describes presenting another person's ideas or code as your own?
questions.hint: It is the most common breach of integrity.

questions.subject: comp
questions.q: Which situation is collusion rather than collaboration?
options: Two students submit nearly identical class structures they wrote together
A student asks the teacher to explain a concept
Students discuss what a client interview is
A student reads the official documentation of a language
questions.answer: Two students submit nearly identical class structures they wrote together
questions.hint: Collaboration is allowed; submitting shared work as individual work is not.

questions.subject: comp
questions.q: You adapted an algorithm from a textbook. The best practice is to:
options: cite the textbook in the documentation and comment the adapted code
rewrite it in another language to hide the source
leave it out of the documentation
questions.answer: cite the textbook in the documentation and comment the adapted code
questions.hint: Adapting is acceptable when it is transparent.

questions.subject: comp
questions.q: Which statement about using an AI assistant during the IA is best aligned with IB expectations?
options: Any use must be acknowledged, and the work submitted must reflect the student's own understanding
AI use never needs to be mentioned
AI may write the entire product if it is cited
Only the teacher may use AI
questions.answer: Any use must be acknowledged, and the work submitted must reflect the student's own understanding
questions.hint: Treat AI output like any other source.

questions.subject: comp
questions.q: A comment placed above imported code to credit its origin is usually called what kind of statement? (one word)
questions.hint: It 'attributes' the code to its author.

questions.subject: comp
questions.q: Why should you test your final files on a different computer before uploading?
options: To catch missing dependencies or paths that only exist on your machine
questions.answer: To catch missing dependencies or paths that only exist on your machine
questions.hint: Think about absolute file paths and installed libraries.

questions.subject: comp
questions.q: Which of these does the teacher do when signing off the IA?
options: Confirms that, to the best of their knowledge, the work is the student's own
questions.answer: Confirms that, to the best of their knowledge, the work is the student's own
questions.hint: This is called authentication.

questions.subject: comp
questions.q: The teacher's feedback on a draft is useful because:
options: it helps you improve, but you must make the changes yourself
the teacher will then rewrite the weak sections
it can be given on unlimited drafts
questions.answer: it helps you improve, but you must make the changes yourself
questions.hint: Who is responsible for the final work?

questions.subject: comp
questions.q: A library performs most of the difficult processing in your product. What is the likely effect on assessment of complexity?
options: Less credit, because the complexity is not the student's own
More credit, because the product is more powerful
questions.answer: Less credit, because the complexity is not the student's own
questions.hint: Credit follows authorship.

questions.subject: comp
questions.q: Your documentation describes a search feature, but the video does not show it working. What should you do before submitting?
options: Make sure the video demonstrates the feature or correct the documentation
Leave it; the moderator will assume it works
Add a screenshot from another project
questions.answer: Make sure the video demonstrates the feature or correct the documentation
questions.hint: Evidence must match claims.

questions.subject: comp
questions.q: Evaluate the use of third-party libraries in a Computer Science IA, considering both the benefits for the product and the consequences for assessment.
questions.hint: Weigh time saved and reliability against how much complexity remains your own.

questions.subject: comp
questions.q: Explain how you would document your use of online sources and AI tools so that your IA meets academic integrity expectations.
questions.hint: Mention where, how and in how much detail you would acknowledge them.

comp-sl.topic: IA: final submission and academic integrity

questions.subject: comp
questions.q: Before submitting your IA, which of these should you check first?
options: That every required component is complete and included
That the code uses the newest language
That the video is as long as possible
That the report has a coloured cover page
questions.answer: That every required component is complete and included
questions.hint: Think about what the moderator needs to see.

questions.subject: comp
questions.q: What term describes being honest about which work is yours and which comes from others? (two words)
questions.hint: The IB has a whole policy about this.

questions.subject: comp
questions.q: You used a free charting library in your product. What should you do?
options: Acknowledge it and explain what it does in your solution
Hide it so the code looks original
Rename its functions so they look like yours
questions.answer: Acknowledge it and explain what it does in your solution
questions.hint: Using other people's code is allowed if you are open about it.

questions.subject: comp
questions.q: Which of these is an example of plagiarism in a Computer Science IA?
options: Copying a sorting function from a website without saying where it came from
Asking your teacher a general question
Testing your code with sample data
questions.answer: Copying a sorting function from a website without saying where it came from
questions.hint: Focus on the missing acknowledgement.

questions.subject: comp
questions.q: Where is the best place to credit a library you used?
options: In the documentation and with a comment in the code where it is used
Only in a message to a friend
questions.answer: In the documentation and with a comment in the code where it is used
questions.hint: A moderator reads both the write-up and the code.

questions.subject: comp
questions.q: What is the general name for code written by someone else that you import to add features, such as a database connector? (one word)
questions.hint: You 'import' it at the top of a file.

questions.subject: comp
questions.q: A classmate offers to send you their working login system to paste into your project. What is the right choice?
options: Politely refuse and build or properly source your own
Accept and change the variable names
Accept but only use half of it
questions.answer: Politely refuse and build or properly source your own
questions.hint: Submitting another student's work as your own is collusion.

questions.subject: comp
questions.q: What word describes two students working together on work that should be individual, and then submitting it as their own? (one word)
questions.hint: It starts with 'coll-'.

questions.subject: comp
questions.q: You followed an online tutorial to learn how to connect to a database. How should you handle this?
options: Cite the tutorial and make clear which parts you adapted
Copy it exactly and say nothing
Ignore it because tutorials don't count
Mention it only in the video
questions.answer: Cite the tutorial and make clear which parts you adapted
questions.hint: Adapting is fine; hiding the source is not.

questions.subject: comp
questions.q: If you used an AI tool to help explain an error message, what should you do?
options: Acknowledge the tool and how you used it
Delete your code and start again
Nothing, because AI tools are not sources
questions.answer: Acknowledge the tool and how you used it
questions.hint: Treat it like any other source of help.

questions.subject: comp
questions.q: Which file check helps make sure the moderator can open your work?
options: Testing that every file opens on another computer
Zipping each line of code separately
questions.answer: Testing that every file opens on another computer
questions.hint: What works on your laptop may not work elsewhere.

questions.subject: comp
questions.q: Why does the IB ask your teacher to confirm the work is yours?
options: To authenticate that the IA is the student's own work
To give extra marks for effort

To choose the client for you

You can keep editing after the deadline
You may swap in a friend's video

questions.hint: 'Final' is the key word.

questions.subject: comp
questions.q: Your video shows a feature that is not in the submitted code. What is the problem?
options: The evidence does not match the product, so it cannot be credited
The video will earn extra marks
The moderator will add the code for you

questions.subject: comp
questions.q: Explain why acknowledging libraries and sources helps both your integrity and the moderator's understanding of your IA.
questions.hint: Think about honesty and about showing which complex parts you built yourself.

questions.subject: comp
questions.q: Describe two checks you would carry out in the last week before submitting your IA, and why each one matters.
questions.hint: Consider completeness, file formats, word count and citations.

questions.subject: econ
questions.q: Which statement best distinguishes economic growth from economic development?
options: Growth is an increase in real output; development is a broader improvement in living standards and well-being
Growth and development mean exactly the same thing
Development is only an increase in exports
Growth includes education and health, development does not
questions.answer: Growth is an increase in real output; development is a broader improvement in living standards and well-being
questions.hint: One is narrower and easier to measure.

questions.subject: econ
questions.q: How many Sustainable Development Goals are there?
questions.hint: Adopted by the UN in 2015.

questions.subject: econ
questions.q: Sustainable development requires balancing which three pillars?
questions.hint: Think beyond income alone.

questions.subject: econ
questions.q: Which of these is NOT one of the HDI indicators?
questions.hint: Recall the three dimensions: health, education, income.

questions.subject: econ
questions.q: Why is GNI per capita measured at purchasing power parity (PPP) in the HDI?
options: To adjust for differences in the cost of living between countries
To include inflation in the index
To remove the effect of population size
questions.answer: To adjust for differences in the cost of living between countries
questions.hint: The same income buys different amounts in different countries.

questions.subject: econ
questions.q: A country has HDI 0.750 and IHDI 0.600. Calculate the overall loss due to inequality as a percentage.
questions.hint: (HDI − IHDI) ÷ HDI × 100.

questions.subject: econ
questions.q: If income, health and education were distributed perfectly equally in a country, its IHDI would be:
questions.hint: The adjustment only lowers the HDI when there is inequality.

questions.subject: econ
questions.q: Which dimension is included in the Gender Inequality Index (GII)?
options: Empowerment, such as share of parliamentary seats held by women
questions.answer: Empowerment, such as share of parliamentary seats held by women
questions.hint: GII has reproductive health, empowerment and labour market dimensions.

questions.subject: econ
questions.q: Which pair of indicators measures reproductive health in the GII?
options: Maternal mortality ratio and adolescent birth rate
Infant vaccination and doctors per person
questions.answer: Maternal mortality ratio and adolescent birth rate
questions.hint: Both focus on women's health outcomes.

questions.subject: econ
questions.q: Country X has GII 0.05 and Country Y has GII 0.55. Which is correct?
options: Country X has greater gender equality
Country Y has greater gender equality
GII cannot be compared between countries
questions.answer: Country X has greater gender equality
questions.hint: For the GII, lower is better.

questions.subject: econ
questions.q: How many indicators make up the global Multidimensional Poverty Index (MPI)?
questions.hint: They are grouped into three dimensions.

questions.subject: econ
questions.q: Under the MPI, a household is identified as multidimensionally poor if it is deprived in at least:
options: one third of the weighted indicators
questions.answer: one third of the weighted indicators
questions.hint: The threshold is a fraction of the weighted indicators.

questions.subject: econ
questions.q: A strength of the MPI compared with an income-only poverty line is that it:
options: shows which deprivations people face, helping to target policy
is based only on household income
questions.answer: shows which deprivations people face, helping to target policy
questions.hint: Think about what policymakers need to know.

questions.subject: econ
questions.q: Two countries have a similar GNI per capita, but Country P has a much higher HDI rank. The most likely explanation is:
options: Country P converts income into better health and education outcomes
Country P has a larger population
questions.answer: Country P converts income into better health and education outcomes
questions.hint: Compare GNI rank with HDI rank.

questions.subject: econ
questions.q: Compare and contrast the HDI and the IHDI as measures of economic development.
questions.hint: Discuss what they share, how they differ, and what extra information the IHDI gives.

questions.subject: econ
questions.q: Using data from a composite indicator, evaluate the view that a single index can accurately measure a country's level of development.
questions.hint: Consider what composite indices capture and what they miss, such as environment or political freedom.

questions.subject: econ
questions.q: Which definition best describes sustainable development?
options: Development that meets the needs of the present without compromising the ability of future generations to meet their own needs
Growth in real GDP of at least 3% per year
Development funded only by foreign aid
questions.answer: Development that meets the needs of the present without compromising the ability of future generations to meet their own needs
questions.hint: Think about present and future generations.

questions.subject: econ
questions.q: How many Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) were adopted by the United Nations in 2015?
questions.hint: It is a number between 15 and 20.

questions.subject: econ
questions.q: By which year are the SDGs intended to be achieved?
questions.hint: They were set for a 15-year period starting in 2015.

questions.subject: econ
questions.q: Which three dimensions does the Human Development Index (HDI) measure?
options: Health, education and standard of living
questions.answer: Health, education and standard of living
questions.hint: One indicator is life expectancy.

questions.subject: econ
questions.q: Which indicator is used for the standard of living dimension of the HDI?
questions.hint: It is an income measure adjusted for purchasing power.

questions.subject: econ
questions.q: HDI values lie between:
questions.hint: A value closer to the top means higher development.

questions.subject: econ
questions.q: What does the 'I' at the start of IHDI stand for? (two words)
questions.hint: It adjusts the HDI for how unevenly development is shared.

questions.subject: econ
questions.q: If a country's IHDI is much lower than its HDI, this suggests:
options: high inequality in health, education and income
questions.answer: high inequality in health, education and income
questions.hint: The gap is the 'loss' due to inequality.

questions.subject: econ
questions.q: What does the Gender Inequality Index (GII) measure?
options: Disadvantage faced by women in reproductive health, empowerment and the labour market
The number of women in a country
questions.answer: Disadvantage faced by women in reproductive health, empowerment and the labour market
questions.hint: It has three dimensions.

questions.subject: econ
questions.q: A GII value of 0 means:
options: the country has a low HDI
questions.hint: For GII, a lower value is better.

questions.subject: econ
questions.q: What does MPI stand for? (three words)
questions.hint: It looks at poverty in more than one dimension.

questions.subject: econ
questions.q: Why is the MPI considered more detailed than income-based poverty measures?
options: It measures deprivations in health, education and living standards at household level
It only uses GDP per capita
It is measured once every 50 years
questions.answer: It measures deprivations in health, education and living standards at household level
questions.hint: Poverty is more than a lack of money.

questions.subject: econ
questions.q: Country A: HDI 0.92. Country B: HDI 0.55. Which statement is correct?
options: Country A has a higher level of human development than Country B
Country B is richer than Country A
Country B has more gender equality
Both have the same development level
questions.answer: Country A has a higher level of human development than Country B
questions.hint: Compare the values directly.

questions.subject: econ
questions.q: A country's HDI is 0.800 and its IHDI is 0.680. Calculate the percentage loss due to inequality.
questions.hint: Loss = (HDI − IHDI) ÷ HDI × 100.

questions.subject: econ
questions.q: Explain one limitation of using GDP per capita alone to measure economic development.
questions.hint: Think about what GDP does not show, such as distribution or health.

questions.subject: econ
questions.q: Using the HDI and one other composite indicator, explain why economists use more than one measure of development.
questions.hint: Consider what each indicator includes and what it leaves out.

en-hl.topic: Learner portfolio: synthesis across areas of exploration

questions.subject: en
questions.q: Which statement about the learner portfolio is accurate?

It is worth half of the final grade
It must be written as one long essay
It is only completed in the final week

questions.subject: en
questions.q: Which portfolio entry demonstrates the highest level of synthesis?

A plot outline of the novel
A note on the author's birthplace

questions.subject: en
questions.q: Which area of exploration would most directly guide a discussion of how a text's meaning changes when read in a different century?

questions.subject: en
questions.q: When synthesising across the course, why should you include non-literary texts as well as literary works?
options: The course and its assessments require engagement with both

questions.subject: en
questions.q: For the HL essay, a strong line of inquiry is:

a broad survey of all texts studied

questions.subject: en
questions.q: What term describes the circumstances in which a text was written? (three words, starting 'context of …')

questions.q: A recurring global issue across your portfolio is surveillance. Which pairing would best support an Individual Oral on it?

A recipe book and a sonnet
A travel blog and a fairy tale with no link to surveillance

questions.subject: en
questions.q: Which reflection best shows 'Readers, writers and texts' thinking?

How the poem echoes a myth

questions.subject: en
questions.q: Why might you revisit early portfolio entries in the second year?

To delete them before the exam

questions.subject: en
questions.q: Discuss how two texts from different areas of exploration present the same global issue in contrasting ways.

questions.subject: en
questions.q: Evaluate the usefulness of the learner portfolio as preparation for both the HL essay and Paper 2.

en-sl.topic: Learner portfolio: synthesis across areas of exploration

questions.subject: en
questions.q: Which of these is one of the IB fields of inquiry for global issues?

a local event that only one text mentions

two poems by the same author
only the texts you liked most

questions.q: What does 'synthesis' mean when reviewing your portfolio?

Rewriting a text in your own words

questions.subject: en
questions.q: Which portfolio entry shows the strongest synthesis?
options: A note comparing how two texts from different eras represent power
A copy of the teacher's slides

questions.hint: Look for connection and comparison.

questions.subject: en
questions.q: Which global issue would best fit the field of inquiry 'Politics, power and justice'?

questions.hint: Look for an issue about power.

questions.subject: en
questions.q: Why is it useful to tag portfolio entries by area of exploration?
options: It makes it easier to find connections and choose texts for assessments
It is required for every sentence
It replaces the need to read the texts

questions.q: In the phrase 'context of reception', what does 'reception' refer to? (one word)
questions.hint: Who receives the text?

questions.q: Which question belongs to 'Readers, writers and texts'?
options: How do language choices shape meaning?
How did a war affect the text's publication?

How was the text translated over centuries?

questions.subject: en
questions.q: Choose one global issue and explain how it appears in two different texts you have studied.

questions.q: Explain how keeping a learner portfolio throughout the course helps you prepare for the Individual Oral.

questions.subject: en_lit

questions.subject: en_lit
questions.q: How is Purple Hibiscus structured?

As a diary written by Papa
In strict chronological order with no flashbacks

questions.hint: Notice the section titles that mention Palm Sunday.

questions.q: Kambili's frequent silence and stammering in the first part of the novel mainly suggest:

that she does not understand English
that she is bored at home

questions.subject: en_lit
questions.q: Papa is a complex character because he is:

questions.q: What is the name of the young priest who encourages Kambili to find her voice?

questions.q: Papa-Nnukwu is important to the theme of identity because he represents:

questions.q: In Heaney's 'Digging', the line 'The squat pen rests; snug as a gun' creates a sense of:

questions.q: What does the final line of 'Follower', 'and will not go away', suggest about the speaker's feelings?

questions.subject: en_lit
questions.q: In 'Death of a Naturalist', the frogs described as 'great slime kings' mark a shift from:

questions.subject: en_lit
questions.q: In 'Personal Helicon', the speaker says he rhymes 'to see myself'. This links poetry to:

Both are set in large modern cities

questions.q: Which literary term describes a story narrated by a character looking back on events from later? (one word)

questions.hint: It makes a variable measurable.

questions.subject: psych
questions.q: Which ethical guideline means participants are told the true aim of the study after taking part?
questions.hint: It happens at the end of the study.

questions.subject: psych
questions.q: A single-blind design means that:
options: the researcher does not know the conditions
the participants do not know which condition they are in
questions.answer: the participants do not know which condition they are in
questions.hint: It reduces participant expectations.

questions.subject: psych
questions.q: Which sampling method asks existing participants to recruit others they know?
questions.hint: Useful for hard-to-reach groups.

questions.subject: psych
questions.q: Which method collects detailed qualitative data through a flexible, guided conversation?
questions.hint: Some questions are planned; others follow the answers.

questions.subject: psych
questions.q: Explain why a matched pairs design might have been chosen for your class practical.
questions.hint: Think about the problems of the other two designs.

questions.subject: psych
questions.q: Describe one strength and one limitation of the sampling method used in a class practical you carried out.
questions.hint: Consider generalisability and practicality.

questions.subject: psych
questions.q: A researcher compares memory scores of two different groups of participants. Which inferential test is most suitable for ordinal data?
questions.hint: Different participants, so the data are unrelated.

questions.subject: psych
questions.q: Which is an example of a controlled variable in a memory experiment?
options: The time given to learn the list
questions.answer: The time given to learn the list
questions.hint: It is kept the same for everyone.

questions.subject: psych
questions.q: Suggest one way to improve the validity of a class practical you carried out, and explain why it would help.
questions.hint: Think about controls, standardised instructions or the sample.
